subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lead-in: eating out; Listening 3.5.1 on favourite restaurants
outcomes: Discuss eating-out experiences and changes in eating habits
Listen to five speakers and note what each one wants in a restaurant
Know how to organise a narrative essay clearly

tf.s: Voice A is looking for special food and efficient waiters.
tf.why: Voice A talks about a French chef, special food and good waiters.

tf.s: Voice B prefers a big, noisy restaurant.
tf.why: Voice B wants a small, quiet, romantic place.

tf.s: Voice C likes buffet restaurants because they are good value for money.
tf.why: Children can eat as much as they want.

tf.s: Voice D ate in an ancient cistern in Istanbul built by the Romans.
tf.why: This unusual place is Voice D's memory.

tf.s: Voice E prefers fast food because of speed.
tf.why: He thinks restaurants waste time and money.

tf.s: Voice B's favourite restaurant is an Italian place in the mountains.
tf.why: It is a romantic Italian place by the sea.

tf.s: A good narrative essay tells events in a clear, logical order.
tf.why: Logical order makes the story easy to follow.

tf.s: The introduction of a narrative essay does not need to interest the reader.
tf.why: A good introduction catches the reader's attention.

tf.s: A takeaway is food you buy and eat somewhere else.
tf.why: You take the food away from the restaurant.

tf.s: 'Value for money' means something is very expensive and poor.
tf.why: Value for money means you get a lot for what you pay.

mcq.q: Why does Voice C like buffet restaurants?
o: Good value for money; kids can eat as much as they want
mcq.why: Buffets suit families on a budget.

mcq.q: What is important to Voice B?
o: Atmosphere: a small, quiet, romantic place
mcq.why: Voice B values the feeling of the place.

mcq.q: What makes a narrative essay easy to read?
o: Events in a clear, logical order and a good introduction
mcq.why: This is the Top Tip for organising a narrative.

mcq.q: Where did Voice D eat in Istanbul?
o: In an ancient cistern built by the Romans
On a boat by the sea
mcq.why: It was a special and unusual place.

mcq.q: A family with four hungry children wants a lot of food for a fair price. Which restaurant suits them, like Voice C?
o: A quiet café with one dish
mcq.why: Buffets give good value and children can eat a lot.

mcq.q: A busy student has only ten minutes for lunch. Which choice would Voice E agree with?
o: A long dinner by the sea
mcq.why: Voice E values speed above everything.

mcq.q: Which is the best first sentence for a narrative essay about eating out?
o: I will never forget the night our dinner arrived on fire!
This essay is about a restaurant.
mcq.why: It catches the reader's attention immediately.

mcq.q: Why does Voice E think restaurants are not worth it?
o: He thinks they waste time and money
mcq.why: For him, speed and saving money matter most.

mcq.q: Voice A wants efficient waiters. What kind of service would Voice A probably dislike?
o: Special food from a good chef
mcq.why: Efficient waiters work quickly and well, so slow service would disappoint Voice A.

mcq.q: Why should events in a narrative essay be in logical order?
o: So the reader can follow the story easily
mcq.why: Clear order helps the reader understand what happened.
